title: Mirkwood Bats + Yawgmoth + Nest of Scarabs: does one activation pay the drain twice?

you: Yawgmoth, Thran Physician (2/4, untapped, no counters)
Insect token A (1/1 black Insect) — already sacrificed to pay the cost of the ability now on the stack
Insect token B (1/1 black Insect, no counters)

stack.object: Yawgmoth, Thran Physician's activated ability — 'Pay 1 life, Sacrifice another creature: Put a -1/-1 counter on up to one target creature and draw a card.' Cost already paid: 1 life paid (you are at 39) and Insect token A sacrificed. Target chosen: Grizzly Bears.

extras.pod_size: Five players — you and four opponents, 160 opposing life in total.
extras.library: You have 60 cards in your library.
assumptions: No player responds to anything; every opponent passes priority throughout.
No permanent enters or leaves the battlefield except as described by the cards named here.
Insect tokens created by Nest of Scarabs are 1/1 black Insect creature tokens with no abilities.
It is your precombat main phase.
extras.note_for_the_resolver: This is verified stack 003's board with the drainer slot changed to Mirkwood Bats — 003 is checker-passed at 7 drains / 28 opposing life WITH its proliferate, on an identical three-body board, so it is the like-for-like comparison. Stack 002 is NOT the same board: it carries an extra body (the Human Soldier token Bastion's own ETB creates, because an enchantment cannot be one), and its headline 28 is its explicit NO-proliferate invariant while this line spends the proliferate. 002's comparable with-proliferate figure is 8 drains / 32. Compare like with like or not at all. Mirkwood Bats reads 'Whenever you create or sacrifice a token, each opponent loses 1 life'. Yawgmoth's cost is 'Pay 1 life, Sacrifice another creature' — paying it with a token IS a sacrifice, which is the whole question. Settle precisely: does one Yawgmoth activation paid with an Insect token give Bats TWO triggers (one for the sacrifice, one for the Nest token created) or one? Note that a counter-KILLED Insect is not sacrificed, so those deaths pay Bats nothing on the sacrifice half. Bats is 2/3. Keep to Bats' trigger condition and the resulting count; do not re-derive stacks 002/003.

scenario.question: Resolve the stack, then run the engine as far as the rules allow. (a) How many Mirkwood Bats triggers does ONE Yawgmoth activation paid with an Insect token produce, and why? (b) Over the whole engine, how many Bats triggers occur in total and how much life does each opponent lose — and state whether that is more than the 28 that stacks 002 and 003 measured on this same board with a death-metering drainer.

steps.action: Fix the reading and restore the trigger the stack picture omits. THE READING: the scenario's board annotates 'Insect token A' as ALREADY SACRIFICED to pay the cost of the ability now on the stack, so the pilot enters this resolution holding exactly one live Insect (token B) plus Mirkwood Bats (2/3) and Yawgmoth (2/4). THE OMISSION: sacrificing Insect A was a sacrifice of a token while Mirkwood Bats was on the battlefield, so Bats has already triggered and that trigger is not shown. Establish precisely when it went on the stack, because the whole question turns on the two halves of Bats' condition arriving at different times. Activating Yawgmoth's ability put the ability itself on the stack FIRST (602.2a) and the activation cost -- 1 life and 'Sacrifice another creature' -- was paid LAST, as the final step of the activation process (602.2b routing to 601.2h). So Insect A was sacrificed (701.21a) while Yawgmoth's ability was already the topmost object on the stack. Nothing happens at the moment an ability triggers; the Bats trigger waits and is put on the stack the next time a player would receive priority (117.2a), which is immediately after the activation completes, and it becomes the topmost object (603.3) -- i.e. ABOVE Yawgmoth's ability.
steps.effect: Stack (top-down): Mirkwood Bats' trigger from Insect A's sacrifice; Yawgmoth's -1/-1 ability targeting Grizzly Bears. You are at 39 (1 life already paid); each opponent at 40. Bats trigger count: 1. This is the sacrifice half of Bats' condition and it is already banked BEFORE Yawgmoth's ability has done anything at all.

steps.action: Yawgmoth's activated ability resolves. Its target is rechecked first: Grizzly Bears is still on the battlefield and unchanged, so it is still legal (608.2b). Put a -1/-1 counter on Grizzly Bears and draw a card. The counter subtracts from power and toughness (122.1a), so Bears is 1/1.
steps.effect: Grizzly Bears: 2/2 -> 1/1 with one -1/-1 counter, toughness above 0, survives. Library 60 -> 59, hand 1. Putting that counter triggers Nest of Scarabs ('Whenever you put one or more -1/-1 counters on a creature, create that many 1/1 black Insect creature tokens'). Mirkwood Bats does NOT trigger on the counter -- Bats meters creation and sacrifice of tokens, not counters and not deaths.

steps.action: ANSWER (a). State-based actions find nothing (Bears is 1/1), the Nest of Scarabs trigger is put on the stack, all players pass in succession per the scenario's stated assumption (117.4), and it resolves: exactly ONE -1/-1 counter was placed, so Nest creates 'that many' = one 1/1 black Insect token (701.7a). Creating it is the OTHER half of Bats' condition, so Bats triggers a second time; that trigger then resolves for another 1 life from each opponent. On the singular wording: Bats reads 'a token', and 603.2c settles both directions -- an ability triggers only once each time its trigger event occurs, but repeatedly if ONE event contains multiple occurrences. So a Nest trigger that placed N counters at once and created N tokens in a single event would trigger Bats N times, once per token; every Nest trigger in this line places exactly one counter and creates exactly one token, so each is worth exactly one Bats trigger. THEREFORE: one Yawgmoth activation paid with an Insect token and placing a counter produces TWO Bats triggers -- one for the sacrifice, one for the creation -- and they are NOT simultaneous and never sit on the stack together. The sacrifice trigger was on the stack ABOVE the activated ability and resolved before it (step 1); the creation trigger did not exist until Nest's own trigger resolved, two resolutions later. An activation paid with a token that places no counter is worth exactly ONE (the sacrifice half only).
steps.effect: Insect token C is created. Opponents 39 -> 38 each. Bats triggers so far: 2 -- and the first Yawgmoth activation is complete, so the answer to (a) is TWO. Your board: Yawgmoth 2/4, Nest of Scarabs, Mirkwood Bats 2/3, Insect B, Insect C. Bears 1/1. Table life removed: 8.

steps.action: The precision that separates this drainer from stacks 002 and 003: a counter-KILLED Insect pays Bats NOTHING. When a -1/-1 counter drops a 1/1 Insect to 0/0 it is put into its owner's graveyard as a state-based action (704.5f). That is a death, and 002/003's drainers meter exactly that. It is not a sacrifice: to sacrifice is for the permanent's CONTROLLER to move it to the graveyard (701.21a), an action a player takes to pay a cost or follow an instruction, whereas 704.5f is the game putting it there automatically. Bats' condition is 'create or sacrifice', so a counter-kill matches neither half. Only the creation half applies to those tokens -- they paid Bats once, when they were made.
steps.effect: Established for the whole engine: every token is worth +1 Bats trigger when created, +1 more only if it is SACRIFICED (to Yawgmoth's cost), and 0 for dying to a counter. Bats is therefore not a strictly better Zulaport Cutthroat; it counts a different set of events.

To sacrifice a permanent, its controller moves it from the battlefield directly to its owner’s graveyard.

steps.action: Establish the engine's bound before running it, and answer the 2/3 question. Each activation spends one body (the sacrifice) and Nest returns at most one, so the loop is body-neutral only while a counter can land on a creature that is NOT one of your own Insects. The available counter sinks are: (i) Grizzly Bears, an opponent's creature -- two counter-placement events, the second killing it, and both are free to you because it is not your body; (ii) Mirkwood Bats itself. THIS IS WHERE THE 2/3 CHANGES THE BOUND. A 1/1 drainer (stack 003's) dies to its first counter and can never be a sink. Bats at 2/3 absorbs TWO -1/-1 counters and is 0/1 -- toughness 1, above 0, so 704.5f does not apply and it keeps draining (122.1a). Those two counters are two extra body-neutral counter events, each worth a free Nest token and therefore a free Bats trigger. A third counter would make Bats -1/0 and kill it, so two is the cap. (iii) Yawgmoth cannot be a sink at all: he is a Human Cleric and has protection from Humans, so his own ability -- an ability from a Human source -- can never target him (702.16b). And 'up to one target creature' permits choosing zero targets (115.6), so the pilot is never forced to put a counter anywhere.
steps.effect: Counter-sink budget: Bears 2 events, Mirkwood Bats 2 events, then nothing but your own Insects (each such event kills a token and pays Bats nothing). The loop is strictly FINITE. Bats being a 2/3 rather than a 1/1 is worth +5 Bats triggers on this board, measured against the same Bats text on a 1/1 body: a 1/1 drainer dies to its first -1/-1 counter and can never be a counter sink, and that board tops out at 8 triggers where this one reaches 13. The +5 enumerates as +2 on the SACRIFICE half and +3 on the CREATION half, which is where it stops looking like a coincidence. THE +2 SACRIFICES, AND THE MECHANISM IS NOT WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE: Bats' first counter slot buys one body-neutral activation; its second slot makes the proliferate worth a second Nest token, which funds the other activation. Only the FIRST of Bats' two counters is a counter an activation aimed at it; the second arrives from the proliferate, which can only grow a permanent that ALREADY carries a counter (step 8), and no Insect of yours can ever carry a -1/-1 counter and live -- so that second counter never had an Insect alternative to be spared from. Nor does this line spare Insects at all: it counter-kills THREE of your own tokens (D, F and H, step 9) where the 1/1 board's best line kills two, and three is forced in every optimal line here, not a choice. What the 2/3 body buys is ACTIVATIONS, not bodies -- the engine therefore runs SIX Yawgmoth activations instead of four, and every activation pays the sacrifice half exactly once, because sacrificing a token IS this ability's cost. THE +3 CREATIONS: two of them are the Nest tokens those two extra activations make (five token-creating activations here against three, since the last activation in either line targets nothing and makes nothing), and the third is the proliferate -- Bats carrying counters gives proliferate a SECOND permanent to grow, so one proliferate yields two Nest triggers on this board against one on the 1/1 board. None of the +5 comes from the counter-killed tokens: those pay the creation half only and are never sacrificed (steps 5 and 9), so no token this line kills with a counter is counted twice.

steps.action: Activation #2, spending the first of Bats' own two counter slots. Pay 1 life, sacrifice Insect B (a token) -- Bats triggers, and by step 1's sequencing that trigger goes on the stack above the ability and resolves first. Target: Mirkwood Bats itself (a legal target -- it has no protection or hexproof, and you may target your own creature). Bats trigger resolves; then the ability resolves, putting a -1/-1 counter on Bats (2/3 -> 1/2, alive) and drawing a card. SBAs are performed and only then is the resulting Nest trigger put on the stack (117.5); nothing dies. Nest resolves, creating Insect D, and Bats triggers on the creation.
steps.effect: Two Bats triggers this activation, exactly as (a) says. Opponents 38 -> 36 each; you 39 -> 38 (1 life paid, no gain). Library 58, hand 2. Bats 1/2 with one -1/-1 counter. Bodies: Insect C, Insect D. Bats triggers so far: 4. Table life removed: 16.

steps.action: Now spend the three Swamps the scenario deliberately supplies -- Yawgmoth's -1/-1 ability costs no mana, so the only mana sink is his second ability: '{B}{B}, Discard a card: Proliferate.' Tap two Swamps, discard a card drawn earlier. Proliferate lets you CHOOSE any number of permanents that have a counter and give each one more of a kind already there (701.34a), so you choose exactly Grizzly Bears and Mirkwood Bats and nothing else. Bears goes to two counters (0/0); Bats goes to two counters (0/1, alive). This is one event that puts a -1/-1 counter on TWO different creatures, so Nest of Scarabs -- 'whenever you put one or more -1/-1 counters on A CREATURE' -- triggers twice, once per creature, by 603.2c's multiple-occurrences clause. SBAs run before those triggers go on the stack: Bears is 0/0 and is put into its OWNER's graveyard (704.5f); Bats at 0/1 survives. The two Nest triggers then resolve one at a time, each creating one token, each paying Bats once.
steps.effect: Two tokens created (Insect E, Insect F) for two mana and a discard, with NO sacrifice spent -- two Bats triggers for free. Opponents 36 -> 34 each; you 38, hand 1, library 58. Grizzly Bears is dead and in opponent A's graveyard; its death pays Bats nothing (step 5). Bats 0/1 with two counters -- its sink capacity is now exhausted. Bodies: Insects C, D, E, F. One Swamp untapped, which can no longer buy anything (proliferate costs {B}{B}). Bats triggers so far: 6. Table life removed: 24.

steps.action: The terminal phase: every external sink is gone, so each remaining activation must aim its counter at one of your own Insects (or at nothing). Aiming it at an Insect is strictly better than aiming at nothing -- the counter-kill itself pays Bats nothing (step 5), but it triggers Nest, and the token Nest makes IS a creation, worth one Bats trigger. So each of these activations is still worth TWO Bats triggers (sacrifice + creation) while costing a net one body. Run it three times. Activation #3: pay 1 life, sacrifice Insect C (Bats trigger), target Insect D; D becomes 0/0, SBAs put it in the graveyard and it then ceases to exist, and only then does the Nest trigger go on the stack (117.5, 704.5f); Nest creates Insect G (Bats trigger). Activation #4: sacrifice Insect E, target Insect F, Nest creates Insect H -- identical shape. Activation #5: sacrifice Insect G, target Insect H, Nest creates Insect I -- identical shape.
steps.effect: Six more Bats triggers across three activations. Opponents 34 -> 28 each; you 38 -> 35 (three more life paid). Library 58 -> 55, hand 4. Bodies fall 4 -> 3 -> 2 -> 1: only Insect I remains. Bats triggers so far: 12. Table life removed: 48. Note the shape: each of these activations kills two of your tokens and makes one, so the engine is now net -1 body per activation and is visibly winding down.

steps.action: Activation #6, the last one, and the two lines the pilot must decline. Pay 1 life, sacrifice Insect I -- a token, so Bats triggers one final time. For the counter, the only remaining creatures are Yawgmoth (untargetable by his own ability, step 6) and Mirkwood Bats at 0/1. Targeting Bats would be a THIRD counter on it: Bats becomes -1/0 and is put into the graveyard by state-based action before the resulting Nest trigger is ever put on the stack (704.5f), so the token that trigger creates would be created with no Bats on the battlefield and would pay nothing -- the option is worth exactly zero and costs the drainer. The pilot therefore chooses zero targets, which 'up to one target creature' expressly permits (115.6): no counter, no Nest trigger, no token. The engine also cannot continue past this: the only creatures left are Yawgmoth, who cannot pay his own cost ('Sacrifice ANOTHER creature'), and Bats, which is not a token -- sacrificing Bats would pay Bats nothing and remove the drainer, so it is declined too.
steps.effect: One final Bats trigger. Opponents 28 -> 27 each; you 35 -> 34. Library 54, hand 5. No tokens remain. Bats triggers: 13. Table life removed: 52.

steps.action: ANSWER (b) and the final state-based-action check. Ledger of Bats triggers, by half. SACRIFICE half -- six tokens were sacrificed to Yawgmoth's cost: Insect A (pre-resolution, step 1), B, C, E, G, I. CREATION half -- seven tokens were created by Nest of Scarabs: C and D from the two activations that used an external/Bats sink, E and F from the single proliferate (two Nest triggers), and G, H, I from the three terminal activations. Six plus seven is THIRTEEN Bats triggers, each draining every opponent for 1 (119.3). Note what did NOT pay: Grizzly Bears' death and the three Insects killed by counters (D, F, H) are four deaths worth nothing to Bats -- but only THREE of those four are what a 'you control' death-metering drainer would have banked, because Grizzly Bears is an opponent's creature. Zulaport Cutthroat (stack 003) reads 'Whenever this creature or another creature you control dies' and Bastion of Remembrance (stack 002) reads 'Whenever a creature you control dies'; the Bears is not a creature you control, so its death does not match either ability's trigger event and neither ability triggers on it (603.2); the word 'you' on each of those objects refers to that object's controller -- you -- and not to opponent A (109.5). They bank the three counter-killed Insects D, F and H, which are tokens you control. The one drainer that would see all four is stack 004's Blood Artist, which is controller-agnostic -- 'Whenever this creature or another creature dies' carries no controller restriction, so the Bears' death does pay it (though it drains one 'target player', not each opponent). Final SBA check: every opponent is at 27, well above 0, so no player loses the game (704.5a); you are at 34 and drew only 6 cards from a 60-card library. Every Insect token that reached a graveyard, whether sacrificed or counter-killed, then ceased to exist (704.5d), which is why nine token deaths leave no trace in any graveyard.
steps.effect: THIRTEEN Bats triggers. Each opponent loses 13 life: 40 -> 27. Total removed from the table: 13 x 4 = 52. Opposing life 160 -> 108 (32.5% of the table). THE COMPARISON, STATED PER SIBLING, BECAUSE THE TWO SIBLING BOARDS ARE NOT THE SAME BOARD. LIKE-FOR-LIKE AGAINST STACK 003: 003 is this exact three-body board with the drainer slot filled by Zulaport Cutthroat, and its checker-passed 7 drains / 28 opposing life is a WITH-proliferate figure, exactly as this line's is -- so this is 13 drains vs 7 and 52 pod life vs 28, +24 life, 86% more. STACK 002 IS A DIFFERENT BOARD AND ITS 28 IS NOT COMPARABLE TO THIS LINE: 002 carries a fourth body, the 1/1 white Human Soldier token that Bastion of Remembrance's own enters-the-battlefield ability creates (an enchantment cannot be a body), and its headline 7 drains / 28 life is its explicit NO-proliferate board invariant while this line spends the proliferate. 002's comparable with-proliferate figure is 8 drains / 32 opposing life, against which this is 13 drains vs 8 and 52 pod life vs 32, +20 life, +62.5%. Both comparisons favour Mirkwood Bats and neither is the other; 002, 003 and this stack are three boards and must never be presented as one result on one board. The margin's reason is structural, not incidental: a creation-and-sacrifice drainer is paid twice by a single Yawgmoth activation, whereas a death drainer is paid once per body, and Bats' 2/3 body adds two free counter sinks that a 1/1 drainer cannot offer. The price is your own life total: Bats gives you nothing back, so you finish at 34 rather than the 42 that 003's Zulaport Cutthroat -- which gains you 1 life per drain -- left you at (002 ends at 42 on its no-proliferate invariant and 43 on its proliferate line). NOT LETHAL, and not close.

final_state.summary: ANSWER (a): ONE Yawgmoth activation paid with an Insect token produces TWO Mirkwood Bats triggers, and they never sit on the stack together. Bats reads 'Whenever you create or sacrifice a token' and a single activation supplies one of each: the sacrifice is an ACTIVATION COST, paid after the ability is already the topmost object on the stack (602.2a, 602.2b -> 601.2h), so the sacrifice trigger is put on the stack ABOVE the ability (117.2a, 603.3) and resolves BEFORE it; the creation does not happen until Nest of Scarabs' own trigger resolves two resolutions later and puts a token onto the battlefield (701.7a). An activation that places no counter is worth ONE (sacrifice half only). Bats says 'a token', singular, and 603.2c settles the plural case both ways: once per trigger event, but repeatedly if one event contains multiple occurrences -- so a Nest trigger that placed N counters at once would create N tokens in one event and trigger Bats N times, though every Nest trigger in this line places exactly one counter and is worth exactly one. Counter-KILLED Insects pay nothing on the sacrifice half: 704.5f is the game putting a 0/0 into the graveyard, not the controller sacrificing it (701.21a), so those bodies pay Bats only once, when they were created. ANSWER (b): THIRTEEN Bats triggers -- six sacrifices (Insects A, B, C, E, G, I) and seven creations (C, D, E, F from the sink phase including two from a single proliferate, then G, H, I). Each opponent loses 13 life, 40 -> 27; 52 life removed from the table; 160 opposing life -> 108. MORE THAN BOTH SIBLING ENGINES -- BUT THEY MUST BE QUOTED SEPARATELY, BECAUSE ONLY 003'S BOARD IS THIS BOARD. Like-for-like against stack 003: 003 is the same three-body board with Zulaport Cutthroat in the drainer slot, and its checker-passed 7 drains / 28 opposing life is a WITH-proliferate figure, exactly as this line is -- 13 drains vs 7, 52 pod life vs 28, +24 life, 86% more. Stack 002 is NOT this board and its 28 is not comparable to this line: 002's board carries a fourth body, the 1/1 white Human Soldier token Bastion of Remembrance's own enters-the-battlefield ability creates (an enchantment cannot be a body), and its headline 7 drains / 28 life is its explicit NO-proliferate board invariant while this line spends the proliferate. 002's comparable with-proliferate figure is 8 drains / 32 opposing life; against that, 13 drains vs 8 and 52 pod life vs 32, +20 life, +62.5%. Never present 002, 003 and this stack as one result on one board. Two structural reasons, and the second is the one that would be missed: a creation-and-sacrifice drainer is paid TWICE per activation where a death drainer is paid once per body; and Mirkwood Bats' 2/3 body absorbs two -1/-1 counters and lives at 0/1 (122.1a, 704.5f), which a 1/1 drainer cannot do -- Bats' first counter slot buys one body-neutral activation, and its second slot makes the single {B}{B} proliferate worth a second Nest token, which funds the other activation. Only the first of the two is an activation's counter event, and it alone is what qualifies Bats as proliferate's second counter-bearing permanent (Bears and Bats both carrying a counter) instead of Bears alone; the second counter is placed BY the proliferate, which can only grow a permanent that already has one, so it was never a counter one of your Insects could have taken instead. The bound is still strictly FINITE, not infinite: Yawgmoth cannot target himself (protection from Humans, 702.16b), Bears absorbs two counters and Bats two, and after that every activation is net -1 body. The cost is your own life: Bats gains you nothing, so you end at 34 where 003's Zulaport Cutthroat -- which gains you 1 life per drain -- left you at 42 (002 ends at 42 on its no-proliferate invariant and 43 on its proliferate line). NOT LETHAL -- 52 of 160 opposing life.

checker.summary: PASS. Mechanical gate OK. All 32 citations across 11 steps fetched in full with lookup-rule and judged against entire rule text: 32/32 SUPPORTED, 0 unsupported / irrelevant / misquoted. Citation count and arrays confirmed unchanged (6+2+2+3+2+3+2+3+2+2+5 = 32 across 11 steps); the two changed fields are steps[6].effect and final_state.summary, and both are correct. I did not take the prior four passes on trust: I wrote my own memoised exhaustive search and independently reproduce 13 Bats triggers for the 2/3 body and 8 for a 1/1, move for move (6 sacrifices + 7 creations = 13, 13 per opponent, 52 pod, 160 -> 108, you at 34, not lethal, 13 a ceiling). THE REWRITTEN MECHANISM HOLDS, and I verified it more strongly than by matching totals: solving the same engine while varying ONLY Bats' toughness gives 8 / 10 / 13 / 15 triggers at 0 / 1 / 2 / 3 counter slots, which is exactly the artifact's per-slot causal story - first slot +2 (one body-neutral activation and its Nest token), second slot +3 (proliferate's second Nest token, which is a body that funds one more activation, which makes one more token). The forcedness claim is exact: enumerating EVERY optimal line, own-Insect counter-kills is invariant at 3 on this board and 2 on the 1/1 board, and sacrifices are invariant at 6 vs 4. iteration_bound_override.reason: Five iterations against RESOLVE_MAX_ITERATIONS=3, and the bound was crossed twice for reasons outside the loop: the decklist changed under this artifact TWICE while it was open (a 3-card swap, then a 10-card Short List swap), each changing cards.json and re-MISSing this routine under a new fingerprint, so passes 4 and 5 opened new loops rather than extending the old one. Every iteration found a REAL defect and every one of them was in the prose or citation layer, never the arithmetic: a comparison that blended 002's no-proliferate board with 003's, a 'four deaths' claim that ignored the 'creature you control' restriction, 603.2g cited for a controller question when its antecedent is prevention/replacement, and a causal mechanism for the +5 that was twice enumerated wrongly. The ANSWER was never in doubt: five independent checkers each wrote their own exhaustive memoised search and all five reproduced 13 as a ceiling, move-for-move. The final pass went further than any before it, solving the engine while varying only Bats' toughness (8/10/13/15 triggers at 0/1/2/3 counter slots) and thereby confirming the per-slot +2/+3 split as a causal decomposition rather than a coincidence of sums.
